craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of commanded speech; vyabhicāri utsāha at omniscience to be spoken. Sanskrit-first: hṛdaya-ādeśa (O-HEART address — kept; row 7, command opens); adhunā (NOW — kept last-word-urgent). Rows: 7 (heart commanded to speak — address IS the verse's act), 1 (‘now’ closes — immediacy last). Close: ‘show the Lord’s hymn — now’. Rupture: semicolon (gain turns to command — won, then spoken). Rejected: dropping O-heart — killed: address commands; ‘proclaim’ for show — killed: darśaya shows (speech made visible). Read aloud: THROUGH-birth-WAND-er-ing-GEARS, OM-ni-SCI-ence IS-won. O-HEART, no-STRAIN … CAUGHT-clear IN-speech, SHOW the-LORD's-HYMN — NOW.

lines: Through birth-wandering gears, omniscience is won. O heart, no strain;
caught clear in speech, show the Lord's hymn — now.
l4.sanskrit_cite: jātyādibhramaṇaparipāṭīparikarair avāptam sārvajñaṃ hṛdaya | tvadbodhaprasarasaraṇībhūtamahasi sphuṭam vāci prāpya prakaṭaya vibhoḥ stotram adhunā

reads_against.argmap: O heart, what now? → Omniscience gained effortlessly; heart bidden to show the hymn in speech.
c1_essence: Omniscience effortlessly gained; heart bidden to speak the hymn.
